title: Disseminated gonococcal infection: prevented by consistent condom use
vignette: A 24-year-old woman comes to the office due to several days of joint pain and a skin rash. She reports migratory pain involving the wrists and knees and painful swelling over the dorsum of the right wrist. She is sexually active with multiple partners and uses no barrier contraception. Temperature is 38.1 C (100.6 F). Examination reveals tenderness along the tendon sheaths of the right wrist and several scattered pustular skin lesions on the extremities. Culture of a lesion on chocolate (Thayer-Martin) agar grows a gram-negative diplococcus. Which of the following is the most effective way to prevent this patient's condition?

clues.text: migratory pain involving the wrists and knees
clues.note: Migratory polyarthralgia/asymmetric arthritis is one arm of the disseminated gonococcal infection triad (with tenosynovitis and dermatitis).

clues.text: multiple partners and uses no barrier contraception
clues.note: Multiple partners without condom use is the key modifiable risk factor for Neisseria gonorrhoeae transmission - and the answer to prevention.
Tenosynovitis (tendon-sheath inflammation) is a hallmark of disseminated gonococcal infection, part of the classic arthritis-dermatitis syndrome.

clues.text: pustular skin lesions on the extremities
clues.note: Scattered pustular/vesiculopustular lesions on the extremities are the dermatitis component of disseminated gonococcal infection.

clues.text: chocolate (Thayer-Martin) agar grows a gram-negative diplococcus
clues.note: A gram-negative diplococcus growing on chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar identifies Neisseria gonorrhoeae, confirming disseminated gonococcal infection.

whatMatters: Migratory polyarthralgia + tenosynovitis + pustular dermatitis + gram-negative diplococcus on Thayer-Martin agar = disseminated gonococcal infection (N. gonorrhoeae). Because gonorrhea is sexually transmitted, the single most effective prevention among the choices is CONSISTENT CONDOM USE (barrier protection). Answer D.
strategy: Identify N. gonorrhoeae, then recall it is sexually transmitted -> barrier contraception (condoms) prevents transmission. Reject options that don't block sexual spread: there is no effective gonococcal vaccine (antigenic variation of pili), antibiotic prophylaxis isn't used for prevention in the general population, and complement screening detects a susceptibility but doesn't prevent infection.

options.text: Empiric antibiotic prophylaxis for all sexual contacts

eliminations.label: Gonococcal vaccine - none exists (antigenic variation)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a hypothetical vaccine against N. gonorrhoeae. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no effective gonococcal vaccine exists because the organism undergoes rapid antigenic variation of its pili and surface proteins, evading immunity. ✅ Correct if: a vaccine-preventable STI (e.g., HPV, hepatitis B).

eliminations.label: Empiric antibiotic prophylaxis for all contacts - not primary prevention
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: giving antibiotics to sexual contacts. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: partner treatment addresses existing infection/reinfection, not primary prevention of transmission; blanket prophylaxis promotes resistance and is not the most effective preventive strategy. ✅ Correct if: expedited partner therapy for a diagnosed case.

eliminations.label: Screening for terminal complement deficiency - detects risk, doesn't prevent
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: testing for C5-C9 deficiency, which predisposes to disseminated Neisseria infection. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it identifies a host susceptibility but does nothing to prevent acquiring gonorrhea. ✅ Correct if: asking why this patient DISSEMINATED (complement deficiency work-up).

eliminations.label: Meningococcal vaccine - wrong Neisseria species
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: vaccine against N. meningitidis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not protect against N. gonorrhoeae (though some cross-protection is studied, it is not a recommended preventive here). ✅ Correct if: preventing meningococcal disease.

reasoning: Migratory arthralgia + tenosynovitis + pustular dermatitis = disseminated gonococcal infection
Gram-negative diplococcus on Thayer-Martin agar confirms N. gonorrhoeae
N. gonorrhoeae is sexually transmitted; barrier protection blocks transmission
mechanism: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a gram-negative diplococcus that grows on Thayer-Martin (chocolate) agar. Local genital infection can disseminate hematogenously to produce the classic disseminated gonococcal infection (arthritis-dermatitis) syndrome: migratory asymmetric polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, and scattered pustular/vesiculopustular skin lesions (an alternative form is purulent monoarticular septic arthritis). Because transmission is sexual, the most effective preventive measure among the options is consistent barrier protection with condoms. No gonococcal vaccine exists - the organism escapes adaptive immunity through antigenic and phase variation of pilin and opacity (Opa) proteins, which is also why prior infection confers no lasting protection. Terminal complement (C5-C9, membrane attack complex) deficiency predisposes to disseminated Neisseria infection but is a susceptibility marker, not a preventive target.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Micro > N. gonorrhoeae: gram-negative diplococcus, Thayer-Martin agar, no vaccine (antigenic variation of pili), disseminated gonococcal infection (arthritis-dermatitis/tenosynovitis), terminal complement deficiency risk.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: The stem asks for the most effective PREVENTION of a sexually transmitted infection - barrier protection.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on tenosynovitis, disseminated gonococcal infection, Thayer-Martin agar, antigenic variation, or terminal complement (MAC)? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: No gonococcal vaccine exists; complement screening detects susceptibility not prevention; partner antibiotics treat, not primarily prevent.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: gonorrhea prevention = condoms; no vaccine (pilin antigenic variation); complement C5-C9 deficiency -> disseminated Neisseria.

memoryHook: Gonococcus changes its coat too fast for a vaccine to catch it - so the condom, not the needle, is what stops it.
